structured_output.situation_summary: New-onset episodic palpitations with HR drift and labile BP since the last cycle, plus new fatigue and mild exertional dyspnea. The most likely working explanations right now are: Treatment-emergent arrhythmia / autonomic effect; Early reduced cardiac reserve / LVEF decline; Anemia, electrolyte (K/Mg) or thyroid abnormality; Tumor-related deconditioning or QT-prolonging co-meds (to exclude).
structured_output.physician_note: The trial team should review ECG, echo, and the HR/BP trend within 24 hours; until then, it is safer to treat this as an early cardiac toxicity signal.
immediate_actions: Start a log today with palpitation duration, HR/BP at the time, and whether chest pressure, dizziness, or shortness of breath appears.
Keep taking metoprolol and blood-pressure medications as prescribed; do not self-adjust the dose.
If palpitations become sustained, or chest pain, fainting, breathlessness at rest, or ankle swelling appears, contact the trial team or emergency care immediately.

Use an ADC-friendly eating pattern right away: small frequent bland higher-protein meals; if diarrhea is present, add oral rehydration solution or lightly salted rice broth; if nausea is strong, move larger liquids and soups to at least 30 minutes before or after meals.

monitoring_plan.what_to_monitor: Heart rate, blood pressure, palpitation duration, exertional dyspnea, and ankle swelling
monitoring_plan.frequency: Log each episode today and recheck at least morning and evening
monitoring_plan.next_checkin: Trial-team or cardiology review within 24 hours

structured_output.nearest_care_instructions: Chest pain, syncope, sustained palpitations > a few minutes, breathlessness at rest, or ankle swelling - urgent contact.
structured_output.guardrail: This page is a patient-facing summary for a clinical-trial safety review scenario. It supports next-step understanding but does not replace emergency care or formal medical judgment.
